source: NYS Historic Newspapers — the correct archive for the soldier-correspondent lead
why_high_value: The family record calls Charles a 'newspaper correspondent.' Soldier-correspondent letters from the 153rd would appear in the Plattsburgh Republican/Sentinel (Clinton Co., his home) and the Montgomery County Republican / Fonda papers (where the 153rd was organized) — all digitized ONLY at NYS Historic Newspapers, which is gated. This is the single most promising unretrieved lead for Charles: a signed wartime dispatch would be a first-person published voice.
handoff_searches: 'C. F. Hubbell' / 'Charles Hubbell' — Plattsburgh Republican + Sentinel + Montgomery County Republican (Fultonville) + Fonda papers, 1862-1865
Browse the Plattsburgh & Fonda papers Oct-Nov 1864 (Cedar Creek aftermath) for a 153rd-NY correspondent letter
1875: a Champlain/Clinton Co. death notice for Charles F. Hubbell (if news returned east)
